books.section: Topic 4.12 African Americans in the Early Republic, B. The Cultures of African-American Communities

stimulus.text:
"We wish to plead our own cause. Too long have others spoken for us. Too long has the publick been deceived by misrepresentations, in things which concern us dearly." — Freedom’s Journal, first issue, March 16, 1827.

The paper was founded in New York City by John Brown Russwurm and Samuel Cornish, the first newspaper owned and run by Black Americans.
stimulus.source_note: Verbatim public-domain quotation from Freedom's Journal, first issue, March 16, 1827. Wording checked against the Library of Congress exhibition text and the Gilder Lehrman transcription of “To Our Patrons.”

source: original; stimulus is a verbatim public-domain quotation from Freedom's Journal (1827)
stem: Freedom’s Journal is best remembered as

options.text: the first newspaper published in New York City
options.misconception: Many papers came before it in New York.

options.text: a paper funded by the American Colonization Society
the newspaper of the 1830 National Negro Convention
options.misconception: The paper began in 1827, three years before the convention.

options.text: the first newspaper owned and run by Black Americans

rationales.A: New York City had newspapers long before 1827. What was new was who owned this one.
rationales.B: Russwurm and Cornish founded the paper themselves. No colonization money stands behind it.
rationales.C: The paper began in 1827. The first National Negro Convention met in 1830, three years later.
rationales.D: No newspaper before it was owned and run by Black Americans. That is what made the Journal a first.
rationales.general:
1. Read the fact. Russwurm and Cornish founded it in New York City in 1827.
2. Ask what was new. No newspaper before it was owned and run by Black Americans.
3. Keep the date straight. It came before the 1830 convention and before Garrison’s Liberator.
Background: The paper reached readers in eleven states and in Haiti, Europe, and Canada.
Remember: “first” claims need a date, so check what came before.
